processing_steps.method: near-rapid solidification via centrifugal casting into a copper mold
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingot (high purity Fe, Mn, Al, C, Cr) remelted by an induction coil; liquid metal poured into a copper mold at a rotating speed of 600 r/min in Ar atmosphere; obtained as-cast strip size (60–80) mm × 60 mm × 2.5 mm.

Annealing at 550 °C for 9 h, applied only to the 3Cr strip as the annealing-time series (Fig. 11). Heat-treatment furnace used for the strips is a vacuum electric resistance furnace. Longer annealing time reduces austenite dislocation density; κ-carbides are mainly precipitated in the first hour of annealing.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: 3Cr strip from the 550 °C annealing-time series; 9 h annealing; each test data supported by more than three tensile specimens.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Fig. 11(a): engineering stress–strain curves for 3Cr annealed at 550 °C for different times; the 550°C9h curve reaches the largest strain (~50%).

yield_strength.value: no significant change with annealing time after 1 h annealing (not numerically quantified)

defects.dislocation_density: gradually decreases with increasing annealing time (9 h lowest of the annealed 3Cr series); superlattice of dislocations/κ-carbides weak

phases_present.morphology: block-like/angular particles dispersed in the austenite matrix

structures.overall_structure: Austenite (γ) matrix with dispersed δ-ferrite second-phase particles (constituent phases remain austenite and ferrite after 550 °C annealing). Annealing at 550 °C progressively reduces the dislocation density in the austenite with increasing annealing time, while the κ-carbide superlattice in the austenite remains very weak in the Cr-containing strip.

unmapped_findings: For the 3Cr strip annealed at 550 °C, κ-carbides are mainly precipitated in the first hour of annealing while recovery (removal of dislocations) requires longer time; longer annealing time may coarsen κ-carbides, so the annealing time should be optimized to balance κ-carbide coarsening and dislocation-density reduction (block b0050).

The plasticity of the 3Cr strip increases gradually with increasing annealing time at 550 °C, but the yield strength does not change significantly after 1 h annealing; the 9 h annealing is the longest time in this series (block b0050).

The 550 °C heat treatments were carried out in a vacuum electric resistance furnace and only the 3Cr alloy was used for the different-annealing-time series (Fig. 11); the 5 h/550 °C data and the tensile table values (YS/UTS/TE) reported elsewhere in the paper belong to the 5 h process, not to this 9 h sample (blocks b0018, b0049).
